citation.authors: Hon KL, Tsang YC, Pong NH, Lee VW et al

record.population: 34 children with atopic dermatitis, Hong Kong (not people of African descent)
record.design: Uncontrolled before-and-after use of a cream and cleanser containing a lipid complex with shea butter extract (a branded product, not plain shea butter)
record.finding: After 4 weeks, itch score fell from 6.7 to 6.0 and the children's dermatology quality-of-life score improved from 10.0 to 8.0, in the group who rated the product good or very good. No control group, so this cannot show the shea did anything.
record.note: Combination product, so shea cannot be isolated as the active. Human data, but it does not test plain shea butter, so it is not counted as evidence for the claim.
